#  12891 - Network Control Technology and Dynamics 2 Modulübersicht  
|  Module Number:   | **12891 - module is no longer offered from WS 2021/22**  |  
| --- | --- |  
| Module Title:  | **Network Control Technology and Dynamics 2**  |  
|  Netzleittechnik und -dynamik 2   |  
| Department:  |  Faculty 3 - Mechanical Engineering, Electrical and Energy Systems   |  
| Responsible Staff Member:  | 
  * Prof. Dr.-Ing. Schiffer, Johannes 

 |  
| Language of Teaching / Examination:  | English  |  
| Duration:  | 1 semester  |  
| Frequency of Offer:  |  Every summer semester   |  
| Credits:  |  
| Learning Outcome:  | On completion of this module, students should be able to: 
  * Model the dynamics of fundamental components in future power systems;
  * Design local control schemes for decentralized renewable generation sources;
  * Design distributed coordination schemes for intelligent power systems using cooperative control algorithms for complex networks.

 |  
| Contents:  | Modeling of power system components and decentralized renewable energy sources; structures of future power systems; decentralized control design; distributed control algorithms; application of distributed control algorithms to power system and microgrid operation.  |  
| Recommended Prerequisites:  | 12906 Network Control Technology and Dynamics 1  |  
| Mandatory Prerequisites:  | None  |  
| Forms of Teaching and Proportion:  | 
  * Lecture / 2 Hours per Week per Semester 
  * Exercise / 2 Hours per Week per Semester 
  * Self organised studies / 120 Hours 

 |  
| Teaching Materials and Literature:  | None  |  
| Module Examination:  | Final Module Examination (MAP)  |  
| Assessment Mode for Module Examination:  | 
  * Written Examination (90 minutes)

 |  
| Evaluation of Module Examination:  | Performance Verification – graded  |  
| Limited Number of Participants:  | None  |  
| Part of the Study Programme:  | 
  * no assignment

 |  
| Remarks:  | No lectures take place.  |  
| Module Components:  |  Lectures Exercises  |  
| Components to be offered in the Current Semester:  |
